CAT.thesis_one_line: The world's biggest construction/mining-equipment maker had a record quarter selling backup generators to data centers, but the stock already prices in growth far above what history or consensus support.
kill_criteria: Two consecutive quarters of Energy & Transportation (or total) revenue growth decelerating below the FY guidance's low end (currently "mid-teens").
Adjusted operating margin falls back below 19% (vs 21.9% in Q2'26) for two consecutive quarters.
Consolidated net debt (excl. Financial Products captive funding) rises materially -- i.e., MP&E-segment debt increases >$1B in a half-year, unlike H1'26's ~flat MP&E debt.
NTM P/E falls below its own 5-year median.
key_adverse_facts: V1 systematic model labels CAT valuation "excessive": implied 10-year growth 29.6% vs consensus FY1 growth 11.2%, base-case 3y annualised return -29.7%, bear case -49.8%.
Financial Products (captive finance) debt rose $1.839B in H1 2026 while MP&E operating-segment debt was essentially flat, i.e. most of the debt increase funds receivables, not operations.
12-month price momentum +69% (Q09 triage's own red flag) -- much of the AI-power-genset re-rating is plausibly already in the price.
data_conflicts: None found between b1/d4 quant inputs and filings this pass; the only tension is between V1's valuation verdict ("excessive") and the triage's bullish framing, and this dossier resolves it by agreeing with V1.
CAT.confidence_in_thesis: medium (filing-sourced Q2'26 operating results are solid; full 8-quarter table, FCF conversion and insider/litigation scan were not rebuilt this pass under the standard time-box, so confidence in the WATCH call is medium, not high)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: V1's reverse DCF implies ~29.6% 10-year growth versus 11.2% consensus; we find no primary-source evidence (backlog is 1-2yr visibility, not 10yr) that supports sustaining that growth rate, so we agree the price is expensive rather than earned.

CAT.scenario_basis: Adopted V1's own reverse-DCF scenario set directly (starting NTM EPS ~$31.0, WACC 9.34%, implied growth 29.6% vs consensus 11.2%); not independently re-derived this pass.

CBOE.thesis_one_line: Dominant U.S. options exchange with a hard-to-copy SPX/VIX franchise, but 2027 growth estimates cool sharply from 2026's volatility-driven pace, so size it small.
kill_criteria: Organic net-revenue growth guidance cut versus the raised mid-to-high-teens FY2026 range.
Two consecutive quarters of Derivatives segment net-revenue growth below 10% YoY.
Consolidated leverage ratio approaches the covenant ceiling (3.50x, or 4.00-4.25x under the step-up); any move above ~2.5x warrants review.
Data Vantage organic growth falls back below "low double digits" for two consecutive quarters.
Forward P/E re-rates above 25x without a corresponding upgrade to multi-year growth guidance.
key_adverse_facts: 2027 consensus EPS growth is only ~5.5% versus ~25% in 2026 (aggregator cross-check), suggesting 2026's growth is largely a volatility/volume cycle rather than a new sustained run-rate.
Stock reportedly down ~28% from a recent high over the trailing month (aggregator), i.e. the market may already be pricing the 2027 deceleration in.
Balance-sheet debt figure sourced this pass is Q1 2026 ($1,443.4m), not Q2 2026 -- a data gap, not a confirmed adverse fact.
data_conflicts: No v4 b1/d4 quant data independently cross-checked against filings this pass for CBOE -- flagged as a data gap rather than a resolved conflict.
CBOE.confidence_in_thesis: low-medium (no V1 valuation anchor exists for CBOE; the reverse-DCF read here is qualitative and several balance-sheet/insider items are aggregator cross-checks, not primary filings, under the standard time-box)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for CBOE (v1_verdict null). Independently, a ~19x forward multiple against 2026 growth of ~25% cooling to ~5.5% in 2027 looks roughly in line with a high-single-digit-to-low-teens normalized growth base case, not obviously above it.

CBOE.scenario_basis: Qualitative estimate (no V1 anchor, no independently rebuilt DCF): starting adj. EPS run-rate ~$3.56/quarter annualised, base case assumes growth decelerates toward high-single-digits per the 2027 consensus signal, forward multiple mean-reverts modestly from ~19x; bear assumes low-volatility regime compresses Derivatives revenue and multiple derates to ~14x; bull assumes Data Vantage re-accelerates and multiple holds ~22x. Low confidence given the missing systematic anchor.

CVX.thesis_one_line: Low-leverage oil major whose newly closed Hess deal is delivering Guyana production growth ahead of plan, priced at a reasonable multiple but still fully exposed to the oil price.
kill_criteria: Net debt/CFFO (or net debt/EBITDA) rises above 1.5x for two consecutive quarters (vs 0.6x now).
Quarterly production growth YoY falls below 5% for two consecutive quarters (vs +20% in Q2'26).
Quarterly dividend is cut or frozen (breaking the 39-year consecutive-increase streak; $1.78/share since Jan 2026).
Share buybacks fall below $10bn/year pace (analyst reference level, not company guidance; H1-2026 $5.7bn) for two consecutive quarters without a stated commodity-price rationale.
WTI sustained below ~$55/bbl for a full quarter (placeholder breakeven trigger pending primary-source Guyana/Permian breakeven data).
key_adverse_facts: Thesis is fundamentally oil-price dependent; Q2'26's beat is partly commodity-price driven and a downside oil shock overwhelms the production-growth story (the triage's own red flag).
Hess integration is 'still early' per triage despite ahead-of-schedule synergy capture -- full operational integration risk remains multi-year.
Post-close status of the pre-close Exxon/Guyana pre-emption arbitration was not independently re-verified this pass -- a data gap on a material, previously contested item.
data_conflicts: None found between triage framing and filings this pass; leverage cross-check (net debt/CFFO 0.6x) confirms rather than contradicts the triage's 'net debt/EBITDA'-style characterization, though the two ratios use different denominators.
CVX.confidence_in_thesis: medium (Q2'26 production/earnings figures are filing-sourced; leverage ratios, buyback/dividend YTD detail, and Hess-arbitration status are aggregator cross-checks or data gaps under the standard time-box)

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: DV12 restatement: equity reverse DCF at 8.9% (5.17% Treasury + 0.9 x 4.14% ERP), 2.5% terminal. Implied 10-year FCF growth is 1.5% on TTM FCF ($27.1bn, Brent about $92-104) and 7.9% on FY2025 FCF ($16.6bn): below base at spot oil, above base at 2025 oil, so in_line. INCLUDE-SMALL unchanged; oil price is the main unhedged variable. (Earlier text used forward P/E only.)

CVX.scenario_basis: Qualitative estimate (no V1 anchor): base case assumes ~$70-75/bbl average Brent, Hess synergies fully realized, dividend growth continues at ~5%/yr, multiple holds ~13x; bear assumes a sustained sub-$55 oil price with dividend frozen and multiple compressing; bull assumes oil >$85/bbl average and continued buyback pace at the top of the $10-20bn range. Low-medium confidence given the missing systematic anchor and un-rebuilt full DCF.
